summary: The explicit caller-supplied 16-byte salt obligation was introduced by the change. The old source exposes only an unsigned-long salt and fixes the other key half to zero; the new source supports all 16 bytes, while the fixed old harness still calls only the legacy setter.

claims.necessity_reason: After the change, explicit 16-byte salt setting is supported within the target's existing pre-parse salt-configuration surface, but the target cannot reach it.

before.requirement: Explicitly supply all 16 hash-salt bytes, including a nonzero first key half, before parsing.
before.reason: The before source stores only an unsigned-long salt and copies zero into the first SipHash key half. The reconstructed preimage has no XML_SetHashSalt16Bytes definition in xmlparse.c.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: The old parser holds only an unsigned-long salt.
The old hash path fixes the first SipHash key half to zero.
The reconstructed preimage confirms no definition of the new setter in this source file.

after.requirement: Explicitly supply all 16 hash-salt bytes, including a nonzero first key half, to a fresh parser before parsing.
after.reason: The new public setter copies caller-supplied 16-byte entropy before parsing. The old harness calls only XML_SetHashSalt, whose after implementation fixes the first key half to zero.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: The new setter is declared publicly.
The harness's legacy setter cannot supply a nonzero first key half.

harness_evidence.dependency_reason: Shows every parser route through the unchanged target helper.

claims.comparison_reason: The tuple is the same explicit 16-byte pre-parse operation on both sides. It was unsupported before and is supported but unreachable through the fixed harness after; the prior unsigned-long limitation is not labeled a preexisting blocker for a capability that did not yet exist.
